Brewers superfan basks in World Series glory
 Elizabeth Flores USA TODAY Updated Oct. 24, 2026, 8:34 p.m. ET Hear this story Amy Williams, known as “Front Row Amy,” is a Milwaukee Brewers superfan recognized for her constant presence directly behind home plate at American Family Field.
 Williams can be found in Section 117, Row 1, Seat 5 at American Family Field, a seat right in front of all the action and directly behind home plate. She typically attends around 40 regular-season Brewers home games each year and is easily recognized for meticulously keeping score by hand for every pitch, a tradition she has maintained for years.
 Williams shares that her journey from her home in Oshkosh, Wisconsin, to American Family Field covers more than 85 miles each way. Despite the lengthy commute, she rarely misses a game in person.
 More: Brewers superfan's World Series wish comes true A mother of three, Williams proudly shared that she has not missed a single Brewers game, whether attending in person, watching on television, or listening on the radio, since May 2007. Williams has also said that she attended 35 games during the 2026 season and is determined to be present at every home game throughout the Brewers' postseason run.

To the delight of Front Row Amy and the entire Brewers faithful, Milwaukee holds a 1-0 advantage in the 2026 World Series after withstanding a dramatic late push from the Tampa Bay Rays to clinch a thrilling 3-2 win in Game 1.
